cases.name: 01-pdf-ali
cases.content:
The acquisition of Tabular by Databricks marks a significant shift for the data ecosystem. It reinforces a core principle: the best technology wins when it is open.

For years, the industry has debated proprietary versus open standards. By bringing together the teams behind Apache Spark and Apache Iceberg, we are doubling down on the belief that openness drives the best outcomes for the customer.

Spark revolutionized large-scale data processing. Iceberg brought similar innovation to table formats, solving difficult challenges in how we manage data. Having these teams work under one roof creates an opportunity to accelerate development across the stack.

This acquisition is about more than just product capabilities. It is a commitment to the open-source model. When infrastructure is open, it prevents lock-in and encourages the type of collaboration that solves complex engineering problems.

Customers need platforms that prioritize interoperability. They want to know their data infrastructure can evolve without being tied to a closed implementation. Our focus is to ensure that openness remains the default for the industry. We look forward to seeing what this partnership delivers for the data community.

cases.name: 02-pdf-matei
cases.content:
The AI industry is moving away from purely chasing larger monolithic models. The next wave of progress is shifting toward compound AI systems. Success relies on how you orchestrate multiple models, retrieval, and tools together, rather than just scaling parameters.
---
Compound systems often outperform monolithic models on complex, real-world tasks. By integrating retrieval and specialized tools, developers can bridge the gap in logic and accuracy. It is about building a system that can reason reliably over proprietary data.
---
This is what we are building toward with Mosaic and our ML platform. We are focused on the infrastructure needed to compose these systems effectively. The goal is giving engineers the environment to orchestrate, monitor, and deploy compound AI applications.

cases.name: historical-disclosure
cases.content:
On February 9, 2026, we disclosed that Databricks surpassed a $5.4 billion revenue run-rate.

It is important to clarify that this figure reflects a run-rate rather than recognized annual revenue. It represents a snapshot of that specific period. Business milestones like this are often viewed as final outcomes, but they may be better understood as consequences of long-term technical foundations.

Durable engineering value is the bedrock of any scaling effort. Our focus remains on the underlying architecture and the systems we build. The technical discipline required to maintain these systems is significant.

When we look back at the development cycles that precede such milestones, it becomes evident that the architecture must be resilient. We have consistently prioritized structural integrity over short-term optimizations. This approach is fundamental to how we build. By placing engineering value at the center of our development strategy, we maintain focus on our core design principles. The run-rate itself is an outcome. The true measure of our progress is found in the reliability of the tools we build.

cases.name: 01-pdf-ali
cases.content:
The acquisition of Tabular is a significant step for the future of data infrastructure. This move validates the open-source approach that has defined our industry for years. Data systems succeed when they prioritize openness, flexibility, and community-driven innovation.

We are bringing the team behind Apache Iceberg into the fold. This unites the engineering expertise behind two of the most critical technologies in the data ecosystem: Apache Spark and Apache Iceberg. These projects have shaped how enterprises manage, process, and analyze data at scale.

When you bring these communities under one roof, you create a unique environment for collaboration. Engineering excellence thrives when it happens in the open. It forces the development of robust, interoperable solutions. This approach avoids proprietary silos that lock customers into a single path.

The best technology wins because it is accessible and scalable. We are moving toward a world where data platforms rely on open standards that encourage integration and stability. This is an exciting milestone for the data community. It reflects a continued commitment to the open ecosystems that power modern analytics.

On February 9, 2026, we disclosed that Databricks surpassed a $5.4 billion revenue run-rate. It is important to be clear that this figure is not recognized annual revenue and does not represent today’s financial result.

Milestones like this often capture attention. Yet, they remain secondary to the durability of the engineering work that sits behind the business.

When we consider the trajectory of the company, we see that financial markers serve as points of reflection. They may provide a snapshot, but they do not necessarily explain the underlying technical efforts required to reach such points. Our focus stays on the substance of the systems we build and the technical challenges we solve. 

The engineering effort is what sustains the work we do. While numbers may fluctuate, the discipline behind the architecture provides the framework for what we are building. It is this focus that allows us to continue moving forward. Durable value is the objective, even if the financial milestones act as a visible, if incomplete, signal of that ongoing progress.

cases.name: team-credit
cases.content:
Our engineering team of 12 has completed the documentation for our open-source parser. We are planning to release these updates next week.

Community reviewers identified areas where the original examples required more clarity. In response, the team rewrote those examples and added a new getting-started guide. This effort ensures that the project remains accessible to everyone who wants to use it.

I want to thank the engineering team for their focused work on these improvements. I also appreciate the community reviewers for their engagement and feedback during this process. Collaboration between engineers and our community is vital for the health of any open-source project. Seeing how we can refine our tools based on these interactions is rewarding. We look forward to sharing these updates with you all next week 🚀.
